Two-input/output projection for AlchemyManager and AC23:14. Full manufacturing fields and execution remain pending.

Public :carnie, :unride/:dismount aliases; GM :town with all 16 legacy destination aliases and :summonall. Travel preserves durable positions, Carnie return points, vehicle inventory/wear, native replies and map acknowledgment. Interaction/loading gates prevent chat bypasses; failed summon recipients are isolated. Remaining GM commands, remaining chat channels and actual-client validation are pending. GM level/lvl, points/sp/statpoint/statpoints, stat/stats, exp and skill overrides now save before replies, use the SQL skill catalog, and reject busy/loading/trading sessions. Direct EXP assignment grants no points; grades are restricted to 1..10 and EXP to uint32. Server chat continuation delivers map/world messages and public party/whisper commands with exact target resolution, preference filtering, loading gates, control/length validation and failed-recipient isolation. Map chat retains AC2:2 without sender echo; additional channels use verified AC2:16 native notices with channel/name text. Command authorization remains intact. Scope is server only; dedicated native channel layouts and guild membership remain pending. Live GM /droprate and :droprate query/update now apply a finite, clamped 0.1–100 process-local multiplier to subsequent victory loot rolls, including active battles. Default 1.0, 35% calibration, 5% floor, disabled rows, native/known item restrictions, captured-monster exclusion and one-entry limit are preserved. World ownership serializes updates and rewards. Deterministic probability, GM authorization/revocation, private native feedback and victory-loot integration tests cover the port. GUI loot editing and actual-client command validation remain pending. GM repair/fixall now clears durability damage on equipped items and bag stacks for self or an online target without payment. State saves before native AC23 removal/addition and equipment replies; quantities, forge metadata and unrelated state remain intact. Missing targets do not fall back to self; actor/target loading, battle, trade, event, storm and beach gates prevent bypasses. Healthy repeats are no-ops; failed persistence publishes nothing, and failed target delivery requires reconnect without disconnecting the GM. Source restored-item feedback counts only damaged stacks. Native-client command acceptance remains pending. GM restat/resetstats now sets each stored base attribute to 10, refunds max(sum(base)-50,0) with uint16 saturation, refills equipped HP/SP and saves before AC8 stat updates and AC5:3 snapshot. Permanent avatar bonuses remain additive and are excluded from refunds: the original bonus-inclusive getters/base setters would mint bonus points on every repeated reset. Missing targets fail explicitly; actor/target loading, battle, trade, event, storm and beach gates prevent bypasses. Skills, level/EXP, currency and inventory remain intact. Regression tests cover repeat safety, ordinary spending of refunds, saturation, native replies, target authorization/revocation, save/snapshot failures and failed-target isolation. Native-client reset acceptance remains pending.

Existing menu teleports and sprite refresh; Carnie menu and public chat travel now share return-point handling that does not alter the previous point after a failed save or unavailable destination. Carnie travel interaction gates preserve loading, battle and event ownership. Script-owned transitions remain unrestricted by chat guards. Actual-client validation remains pending.
Inbound handlers and interaction policies now share one registry; exhaustive raw opcode tests preserve existing routing and gate exceptions. Migration status is unchanged.

Character and client-slot pet stat allocation implemented, including stat-qualified character skills and grade-ten evolutions. Attributes and skills commit together before updates; HP/SP are not refilled. Budget/wrapping, persistence and failed-save regressions pass.

All five reference operations implemented: immediate same-map add, accept/decline, list, removal and status query. Contacts share the durable symmetric AC14 store, both list limits and deletion cleanup. Native AC10:1 status and AC10:4 removal receipts preserved; lists publish one authoritative AC14:11/5 snapshot instead of duplicated in-memory/database lists. Malformed requests, world gates, stale invitations and failed persistence/recipient writes covered. Native-client capture acceptance remains pending.

Three draws per character per UTC day; SQL-weighted rewards and usage commit atomically against fresh durable state. Native client capture confirms inbound AC104:1. Fresh translated aLogin.exe Lottery handlers recover outgoing AC104:1:1 catalog and AC104:1:2 result with cumulative used counts, superseding the C# constant-one and AC35:12 balance assumptions. Catalogs synchronize at login, warp, menu refresh and UTC midnight. SQL slots are consecutive in authored order, at most 20. Independent packets, reconnect/refresh, capacity, rollback, receipt failure and clock-reset regressions cover gameplay and display state. Bounded draw-specific diagnostics preserve credentials. Fourteen equal-weight reference outcomes remain; paid draws/global announcements remain unported, the user confirmed corrected rewards, allowance and refresh/reopen in the original client. A fresh character completed three live spins with captured cumulative usage 1/2/3.

AC14 friendship requests/accept/removal/lists and native text mail implemented. Text mail persists with verified identities before ACK, preserves native encoded bytes, delivers across maps and queues offline/loading recipients for AC12 publication. Schema v6 cascades sender/recipient deletion. Delivery markers follow successful socket writes; crash-boundary duplicates remain possible. Name fallback, parcel/attachment mail, actual-client validation remain pending. Native AC10 contact commands now share these durable relationships; same-map immediate add semantics remain separate from AC14 invitations.

Native rename (raw ASCII), permanent party release and companion mount/rest implemented. Client slot/alias validation, durable changes before broadcasts, owner/peer snapshots and removal cleanup covered. Vehicle/raft placement, boarding, landing and ACK subcodes are implemented with exact-slot validation, durable mutation, wear/wrecking and map synchronization. Item locks and actual-client verification remain pending. Top-level AC15 dispatch is covered by companion control and vehicle regressions.
Native preference packets, persistence and login snapshots implemented; walk/follow acknowledgment behavior preserved. Native-client validation pending.
Rest and native hotel deposit/withdraw/exchange implemented; decoder, full-list exchange and SQLite persistence regressions pass. Native-client validation pending.

Native preference packets, persistence and login snapshots implemented; walk/follow acknowledgment behavior preserved. Native-client validation pending. Native alogin compatibility correction: AC33:2 now supplies four option values, channel mask at payload byte 6 and a trailing no-op byte (eight bytes total). The original six-byte C# ToArray misplaced the mask and disabled native Local chat with the misleading Whisper is closed error. Native receive trace 0x2ea812..0x2ea872 and FUN_002823ac/FUN_00482abc establish offsets and unchanged 1-based channel bit order. Unresolved option 10 keeps native constructor enabled default; tail is zero. Golden tests cover defaults, disabled channels and independent per-bit native decoding; settings refresh and login persistence expectations updated. The user confirmed Local chat works in the real alogin client after restarting and logging in again.

Native AC34:1 balance query implemented for both accepted mode bytes. One authoritative SQL snapshot produces AC75:3/9 balances and AC35:4 checkout resume; no catalog/settings refresh clears the pending cart. Source behavior uses ordinary IM points in both modes; their separate meanings remain unresolved. Read-only query does not spend points or mutate inventory. Raw packet, current-SQL/cache, cart continuation, validation, world gates, read/socket failure and wire-range tests added. Actual-client checkout capture acceptance remains pending.
AC36 bag-slot repair, wrench-first/500 gold payment and same-map effect; fixes missing damage restoration and commits before receipts. Item locks and original-client validation remain pending.

Source audit during the travel-command continuation found that the recorded sha256 differs from both the pinned revision and current sibling file. Both source versions match; their CRLF-normalized SHA-256 is 68c77291de9752a7dd5917f150e91cb4ccfea81c0e156ddb03f032b076c4bbf8. The original recorded hash is preserved for investigation. This handler remains pending.

Recipe-only two-slot AC40 synthesis with symmetric precedence, native status replies and atomic ingredient/output persistence from SQL assets. Strict requests and ownership gates; original-client validation remains pending.

AC45:8 bank/wallet balance, :9 deposit and :10 withdrawal implemented. BankGold persists in the existing character JSON, defaulting to zero for older state. Both balances save before AC26:4 wallet and native AC45 receipts. Checks prevent bank uint32 overflow, carrying-limit loss, insufficient funds and zero transfers. Loading/battle/trade/event gates and failure/reopen tests cover ownership and atomicity. Reference PIN and character-transfer success-only placeholders remain unavailable; verified native ATM activation/capture acceptance remains pending.
Native EVE minigame start/result/finish and outcome routing implemented; native rabbit rewards and restart smoke pass. Standalone arcade rewards and native-client validation pending.

AC67 feeding continuation implements subcommand 1 with a WORD item-ID request and native success/failure receipt. It selects the first registered party pet marked for battle, scans matching bag stacks in slot order and uses shared status-64 feeding with one-item consumption. SQL item definitions supply additive amity gains and the 100 cap; exact-stack metadata and other pets remain intact. Food/amity state commits before remove/stat/banner/receipt packets. Shared feeding rejects bad slots, zero count and empty stacks. Authored wire bytes, client/persistent slot differences, aliases, caps, missing pet/food/definitions, interaction gates and failed-save isolation are covered. Item locks and actual-client AC67 capture validation remain pending.

AC68 stat-allocation continuation implements subcommand 2 with per-login client-slot selection and STR/CON/INT/WIS/AGI selectors. One unallocated point is spent through the shared pet allocator; derived vitals normalize without refill before durable commit, then AC8:2 progression and AC68 receipts are emitted. Invalid/unknown slots, selectors, insufficient budgets and attribute overflow receive failure results rather than the reference default success. Tests cover authored wire bytes, all selectors, alias/persistent-slot distinctions, AC8 budget sharing, reconnect state, interaction gates and save failure. Subcommand 1 remains an explicit unavailable result: the C# potential branch increments without checking or consuming an item and SendPetProgression sends level-minus-one as stat 37, so genuine potential-item and client-display semantics remain unverified.

AC69 rebirth ascension continuation implements client-slot party-pet selection, level/amity 100 requirements, level-1/zero-EXP reset, 50 additive stat points and reborn metadata while retaining attributes, skills, equipment, job and active-pet selection. Vitals normalize/refill before durable commit; success/list/progression packets follow the save. Repeat/ineligible/unknown slots fail without mutation; malformed/unknown subcommands, overflow, save failure and loading/battle/trade/event/cutscene gates are covered. Native client AC69 capture validation and model/quest-driven evolution remain pending.

Points/bonus catalogs, balances and atomic cart purchases; Strong Scroll upgrades and 50% point forging with atomic costs and native AC75:6 replies; AC75:4 category forwarding with the legacy zero seed and authoritative balance refresh. All defined AC75 request handlers are mapped. Arcade ticket/prize exchange and original-client validation remain pending.
Native read-only contents request/response and cache hints implemented; original-client validation remains pending.
Inbound handlers and interaction policies now share one registry; exhaustive raw opcode tests preserve existing routing and gate exceptions. Migration status is unchanged.

Inbound handlers and interaction policies share one registry with raw opcode routing tests. AutoSaveLoop ports the one-second character checkpoint and adds a final disconnect checkpoint. Pending snapshots commit transactionally only against their previous checkpoint; unchanged/already-durable snapshots skip writes, newer durable state conflicts without being overwritten, and deleted characters are never recreated. Warping presence is included, failures are isolated per character, and cancellation is bounded. Account IM/bonus balances already persist transactionally on mutation and are never copied from session caches. Remaining WorldServer login/quest/session-handoff and native-client acceptance work is pending.

GUI loot editing and actual-client command validation remain pending.

PvE proficiency/evolution and durable battle reward completion implemented. Captures/desertion stage roster changes and peer broadcasts until commit; failed saves abandon and disconnect without departure success. Parties, monster skill AI and other combat parity remain partial. Explicit SQL skill-ID dispatch corrects Shrink/Hot Fire fallback damage. Battle-only effective stat reductions, non-compounding refresh/expiry, ally damage buffs, strict effect targets and durable proficiency are tested. These correct gaps inherited from the C# name classifiers; the duration/magnitude compatibility policy is documented in PORTING.md. Native hit-chance, persistent visual status and complete Goddess parity remain pending. Generic effect continuation replaces the earlier skill-ID dispatch and numerical status checks with declarative skill effects, native layer/code projection and aggregate stat/damage modifiers. Buff groups, refresh/expiry, temporary speed, player/pet/monster effects, arbitrary multi-effect abilities and SQL/native parity are tested. Native magnitudes/durations retain the documented compatibility policy; remaining control-status decoding and full original-client parity are pending. Control continuation removes separate StatusKind/Status storage and skill-name condition classifiers. Declarative action blocking, damage-sensitive removal, periodic HP damage, ally attack redirection, on-hit application and timed presentation now use ActiveEffect. Recognized native condition classes load from SQL; generic/native/server tests cover blocking, waking, DOT knockout, expiry, redirection and durable control proficiency. Vanish is a presentation effect preserving existing gameplay; native protection/resistance and secondary-hit decoding remain pending. Vanish protection continuation adds generic miss_physical_attacks and miss_area_attacks capabilities, confirmed by user investigation and translated native description. Player, pet, combo and monster attacks emit zero-damage miss records without applying hit effects; SP and proficiency still count. Native targeting pattern bytes now project from SQL and offline decoders; grade bands 1-3/4-6/7-9/10 are compatibility assumptions with an authored area_attack override. Complete AOE target expansion, native grade thresholds and original-client MISS rendering remain pending. Stone Wall continuation maps protection layer 4/code 101 to ally-targeted miss_physical_attacks using the shared effect engine. Physical attacks miss; single-target and area magic remain damaging. Existing metadata duration policy, SP cost and proficiency persist. Native/arbitrary-ID battle and installed-SQL tests cover ally targeting, non-damaging casts, physical immunity, allowed magic, expiry, miss/support packets and durable proficiency. Water Shield continuation narrows protection layer 4/code 105 to magical_damage_taken (-50 percent). Generic incoming reduction and applicable magical modifiers aggregate once with the existing group policy and single rounding step; physical/basic/staff/monster attacks and periodic damage remain unchanged. Native projection, arbitrary-ID attack/stacking/expiry tests and an installed-SQL cast with unreduced physical retaliation and durable proficiency pass. Party combo continuation replaces pair-only scheduling and damage batches with full-party single-target speed chains (adjacent effective SPD gap at most 99). Round speed snapshots, support/enemy ordering barriers, SQL grade-aware area exclusion and execution-time bridge revalidation preserve action order. Eight player/pet hit records share one animation and aggregate damage; each actor retains SP cost and durable proficiency. Combat regressions and a three-player server persistence test cover chains, boundaries, barriers and lost/redirected bridges. Saved community evidence and remaining deterministic level-chance policy are documented in COMBOS.md; Burst EXP remains outside scope. Combo probability continuation implements the user-requested clamped linear curve from 0 percent at party mean minus enemy level of -25, through 50 percent at equal levels, to 100 percent at +25. Whole present player/pet roster averages retain fractional levels and include support/knocked-out fighters, excluding absent fighters. Each eligible chain rolls once against its actual target; failure executes singles without bonus or subset rerolls. Endpoints and singles consume no chance rolls. Probability, roster and failure damage tests cover this compatibility policy; native formula and rebirth level offsets remain unverified. Rebirth combo continuation implements the user-specified +99 effective levels for each reborn player/pet before party averaging and for reborn targets. Characters carry optional durable reborn metadata and pets retain their existing flag. Effective levels use int arithmetic without altering byte-sized visible levels or stored EXP. Mixed-party means, absent reborn pets, high-level overflow and target parity tests pass; three reborn level-1 players combo against a level-75 enemy and retain flags and skill proficiency through battle saves. Full character rebirth progression, job and roster presentation remain pending. Shield Defense continuation maps native buff layer 19/code 52 to physical_damage_taken (-50 percent), preserving SQL SP/duration and generic effect dispatch. Shared incoming damage aggregation now selects physical or magical protection for every attack, including ordinary and redirected monster basic strikes. Both shields coexist and generic modifiers retain strongest-group and single-rounding semantics. Projection/validation, attack category/expiry/DOT matrices, mixed player/pet combo records, monster redirection, stacking and installed-SQL durable casts are covered. Source asset description is preserved unchanged. Skill/effect JSON TODO continuation adds source-only effect_refs annotations, reusable skill_effects.json definitions and JSON schemas. SQL indexes and resolves authoritative definitions/ref rows, with clone isolation, explicit-empty/inline semantics and invalid-reference rejection. Export/manifest/reconstruction verification preserves native bytes and provenance; the asset database is rebuilt separately with backups. Shield Defense now increases DEF and MDEF by 10 percent through modifiers, superseding physical reduction, preserving cost/duration and durable proficiency. Reference validation, SQL row edits/deletion, category/stat/expiry and installed catalog tests cover the new policy. Data-driven conversion continuation removes ability-specific Go constants and switch branches. Authored internal/assets/native_effect_rules.json supplies layer/code mappings and effect templates to offline decoders/exporters; generic validation, cloning and native duration adjustment remain in Go. Runtime SQL requires explicit effects or references and never infers native effects. JSON-only new mappings/tuning, template isolation, invalid rules/durations and missing SQL metadata are covered.
